title: API 580 Training in San Francisco Bay Area: RBI Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 580 risk based inspection exam prep for Bay Area RBI teams: county safety ordinance, renewable conversions, hydrogen plants. Instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training in the San Francisco Bay Area: Online RBI Exam Prep for Inspection Planners, Engineers and Inspectors
html:
API 580 exam prep for Bay Area RBI teams

Risk-based inspection work in the Bay Area is done by small groups of people who know a plant's equipment in detail: inspection planners, corrosion and materials engineers, reliability engineers, process engineers who understand what each circuit actually carries, and certified inspectors who bring field evidence into the assessment. This page is for anyone in that circle around Richmond, Rodeo and Martinez who is preparing for the API 580 Risk Based Inspection examination, whether they already hold API 510, 570 or 653 or are coming to it from engineering.

There is no Atlantis classroom in the San Francisco Bay Area for RBI candidates to attend, and there is no Atlantis office in San Francisco, Richmond or anywhere else in the region; Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad, and the API 580 course is self-paced online study with an instructor who answers your questions. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the examination and issues the certification. API's page for the API 580 programme says the exam can now be scheduled at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and the course is preparation for API's exam, not a route around it.

Where risk-based inspection work sits around the bay

Contra Costa Health's list of facilities under the county's Industrial Safety Ordinance is a good map of where Bay Area RBI people work. It names Martinez Refining Company, PBF Energy's plant on the former Shell site; Martinez Renewable Fuels, the former Marathon refinery now run as a renewable fuels joint venture with Neste; the Phillips 66 Rodeo facility, which now runs on renewable feeds; two Air Products hydrogen operations inside the Martinez sites; and the Air Liquide hydrogen plant at Rodeo. Richmond's own ordinance covers Chevron's Richmond refinery, which EIA lists at 245,271 barrels per calendar day of crude capacity as of January 2026. Beyond the fences sit pipeline and terminal operators, inspection contractors, and engineering firms that support owners' programmes.

Owners differ in how they rank risk. Some run quantitative programmes built on the API RP 581 methodology, some use semi-quantitative or qualitative methods, and others mix approaches between unit types. The API 580 exam does not test any one site's method or software. It tests the framework in API RP 580, which the 2026 Body of Knowledge lists as the Fourth Edition with Addendum 1, and that framework is what lets an engineer from one plant read another plant's RBI documentation and know what to look for.

What the county ordinance asks, and what an RBI team brings to it

Contra Costa's ordinance extends California's Accidental Release Prevention programme for refineries and chemical plants in unincorporated areas. Contra Costa Health sets out what it adds: the whole facility is covered, not only the processes above a threshold quantity; a Safety Plan is filed as a public document; a human factors programme is required; inherently safer technologies and systems have to be considered; management of change extends to changes in the operations and emergency response organisations; and root cause analysis is required for major accidents or releases. The county audits each covered facility every three years. Chevron's refinery answers to Richmond's version, Chapter 6.43 of the Municipal Code, which the county describes as identical. The refineries also work under Cal/OSHA's refinery process safety standard, section 5189.1, which requires damage mechanism reviews.

None of those rules mentions API 580 or requires risk-based inspection by name. What they do require is evidence that the owner understands how its equipment can fail and has an inspection programme to match, and that is where an RBI team's documents earn their place. A credible assessment names each damage mechanism and why it applies, records the data behind each probability of failure, explains the consequence model, and shows which inspection or mitigation action addresses which risk driver. RBI documentation is one of the ten knowledge areas in the API 580 Body of Knowledge, and candidates who have helped a site prepare for a county audit should find that part of the exam familiar.

Renewable feeds and the probability side of the model

Two of the region's former refineries now process fats, used cooking oil and vegetable oils. Phillips 66 stopped processing crude at Rodeo in early 2024 and Martinez Renewables reached full capacity by the end of that year, according to Argus and Marathon respectively, and project descriptions show both reusing existing hydroprocessing units. For an RBI team, a conversion is the clearest possible case for reassessment: the fluid, the contaminants, the temperatures and the water balance all change, so damage mechanisms selected for petroleum service may no longer apply and new ones arrive.

A 2023 Inspectioneering article on converted units lists the new arrivals: fatty acid corrosion in stainless grades without molybdenum, chloride-driven attack that is worse with used cooking oil, carbon dioxide corrosion where water condenses in the effluent train, and the familiar high temperature hydrogen attack and creep in the reaction section, with polythionic acid stress corrosion cracking and brittle fracture during downtime. It suggests integrity operating windows as part of the answer. In RP 580 terms that means revisiting the damage mechanism screening, resetting the probability of failure for circuits whose history no longer predicts their future, and setting operating limits whose breach should itself trigger a reassessment. The exam asks about reassessment in general terms, but a candidate who has lived through a conversion will recognise what the questions are getting at.

Consequence of failure on a crowded shoreline

RP 580 separates the probability of failure from its consequence, and Bay Area sites show why the consequence side cannot be copied from a plant somewhere else. The refineries and hydrogen plants sit on the shore of San Pablo Bay and the Carquinez Strait, close to homes, roads and rail lines, so safety and environmental consequences of a release carry weight. Business consequences carry weight too: with Benicia no longer refining, two of the crude refineries on EIA's January 2026 list are left in the region, and an unplanned outage at either matters well beyond its own fence.

The exam tests the concepts rather than any local figures: how consequence is assessed for flammable, toxic and environmental releases, how inventory, isolation and detection affect the result, and why inspection changes the assessed probability of failure but leaves the consequence untouched. To reduce consequence, an owner changes something physical or operational, such as the inventory held, the speed of isolation or the detection system. A question that offers more inspection as a way to cut consequence is usually testing whether you know that.

Hydrogen plants, pipelines and the edges of an RBI scope

The county's list shows how often the equipment inside a refinery fence belongs to someone else: the hydrogen units at both Martinez sites are Air Products operations, and Rodeo's hydrogen plant is Air Liquide's. When a supplier owns the hydrogen plant, the RBI boundary, the data, the inspection history and the consequence model may sit with a different owner from the refinery around it, and the interfaces between them need to be agreed rather than assumed. RP 580's treatment of the RBI team and the scope of an assessment is directly relevant.

Pipelines have a boundary of their own. Kinder Morgan's 2025 brochure describes the breakout tankage at its Concord station, where lines to Sacramento, Fresno and San Jose begin. Federal pipeline rules currently prevent operators from using the risk-based procedures in API 653 to set the internal inspection interval of a breakout tank, and a PHMSA proposal published in June 2026 to allow it, with maximum intervals, had not become a final rule at the time of writing. An RBI candidate at a terminal company should know which of its tanks sit under that rule.

Closed-book practice: questions to answer without the book

API 580 is entirely closed book, so concepts have to be learned until you can explain them in your own words. Try these before looking anything up:

  1. Why can two identical exchangers, built from the same drawing, carry different risk? Because consequence depends on the fluid, inventory, location and people nearby, and probability on the service and history, not on the drawing.
  2. What does inspection change in a risk assessment? It reduces uncertainty about the actual damage state, and so the assessed probability of failure; it does not change the consequence.
  3. When must an assessment be revisited? After significant changes in process conditions, feed, equipment or damage mechanisms, after inspection findings that contradict the model, and at intervals the owner sets, rather than only when software prompts it.
  4. What makes an inspection more effective for a given mechanism? Choosing a technique able to detect that mechanism, covering enough of the area where it occurs, and timing it before the damage becomes significant. A thickness survey cannot find a cracking mechanism, however many points it takes.
  5. Who belongs on the RBI team? People with knowledge of inspection, materials and corrosion, process, operations and risk assessment, with an RBI team leader responsible for the work, as RP 580 describes roles and responsibilities.

Who sits API 580 here, and how they qualify

A current API 510, 570 or 653 certification qualifies you automatically, so certified inspectors at Richmond and Martinez can move straight to the application. Everyone else qualifies on education and petrochemical industry experience gained in the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more without formal education. That opens the exam to engineers who have never held an inspector certificate, such as process engineers at the renewable fuels plants or corrosion engineers at the hydrogen suppliers. The exam has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 of them scored, over 3.25 hours.

Remote proctoring helps Bay Area candidates who would otherwise spend half the day crossing bridges, but it brings its own conditions about the room and the equipment you use, so read API's and the proctoring provider's requirements well before you book. If you prefer a test centre, Prometric lists centres in and around the Bay Area.

When a site needs an RBI study rather than an exam

Exam preparation teaches the RP 580 framework; it does not produce an assessment of your equipment. Owners who want a risk-based inspection study carried out, revalidated or audited can see Atlantis's risk-based inspection services, which are delivered remotely from the owner's data and the owner's inspection records. The owner's inspector of record still approves the intervals, and Atlantis does not offer fitness-for-service assessments. For the course itself, see the API 580 training overview.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a Bay Area site

RBI teams are mixed by nature, and so are the groups that sponsors enrol: a certified piping inspector beside a process engineer, or a corrosion engineer beside a terminal integrity specialist. Each candidate studies at their own pace and sends questions to the instructor as they arise, and fees are quoted on request. Each person applies to API individually, so confirm who qualifies automatically and who needs to document experience before you enrol them, and tell us whether any of the group are also preparing for API 510, 570 or 653.

faq.q: Can a Bay Area candidate take API 580 by remote proctoring?
faq.a: API's programme page for API 580 says the exam can now be scheduled either at in-person test centres or through remote proctoring. That is a difference from API 510, 570 and 653, which are held in person at Prometric test centres. If you choose remote proctoring, check the room, computer and identification rules well before your appointment so that a technical problem does not cost you the attempt.

faq.q: Does the Contra Costa Industrial Safety Ordinance require risk-based inspection?
faq.a: The county's descriptions of the ordinance do not mention risk-based inspection or API 580. They describe a Safety Plan, a human factors programme, consideration of inherently safer systems, management of organisational change, root cause analysis and county audits every three years, on top of the CalARP programme. RBI is one way an owner can show that its inspection programme matches its damage mechanisms, but the choice of method is the owner's.

faq.q: Our hydrogen plant is run by a gas supplier inside the refinery fence. Whose RBI programme covers it?
faq.a: Usually the supplier's, because the supplier owns and operates the equipment, but the answer depends on the contracts and on how the sites divide their process safety programmes. Contra Costa Health lists the Air Products units at both Martinez sites and Air Liquide's Rodeo hydrogen plant as covered facilities in their own right. The interfaces, such as shared lines and utilities, are where RBI scopes most often leave gaps.

faq.q: How do renewable feeds change an RBI assessment?
faq.a: They change the damage mechanisms that apply and make the old corrosion history unreliable. Fatty acid corrosion, chloride effects from used cooking oil and carbon dioxide corrosion in the effluent train join the familiar hydroprocessing mechanisms, so the screening and the probability of failure have to be redone. Integrity operating windows help keep the new assessment honest once the unit is running.

faq.q: I am a process engineer with no inspection certificate. Can I sit API 580?
faq.a: Yes, if you meet API's education and experience scale. With a bachelor's degree you need one year of petrochemical industry experience in the last 10 years; with a two-year degree, two years; with a high school diploma, three. You document the experience in your application. Process engineers may find the consequence and data sections easier than inspectors do, and the damage mechanism sections harder.

faq.q: Is the quantitative API RP 581 method on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: The 2026 Body of Knowledge lists API RP 580 as the reference for the exam, and the questions test the RP 580 framework rather than RP 581's calculation procedures. You should still understand where a quantitative method fits among qualitative and semi-quantitative approaches, because RP 580 discusses that choice. Some owners use software built on RP 581, but the exam does not test any software package.

faq.q: Will the course teach me to run our site's RBI software?
faq.a: No. The course prepares you for API's closed-book exam on the RP 580 framework: terminology, risk assessment, the RBI programme, roles, data, damage mechanisms, probability and consequence of failure, risk management and documentation. Software training belongs to the vendor or your employer. Understanding the framework does make it easier to question what a software model is doing with your data.

faq.q: Can an employer enrol a mixed group of inspectors and engineers for API 580?
faq.a: Yes. Each candidate works at their own pace and sends questions to the instructor, so certified inspectors and engineers can prepare together even though they start from different places. Fees are quoted on request. Remember that inspectors with a current API 510, 570 or 653 qualify automatically, while engineers must document their experience, so their applications to API take different paths.
